title: NTT's Robot AI That Predicts Falling Boxes

opening.show: We have five stories today, from robots to 3D graphics, so let's jump right in.

news.label: NTT's AI predicts stack collapses
points: Useful for grasp and placement planning
details: A physics control adapter that handles weight, orientation, and speed is built into a video generation model, so it can evaluate several candidate actions in advance.
In shelf stacking tests with a small robot, the task success rate rose from 73.1 percent to 92.3 percent.
Instead of judging by how a video looks, it predicts outcomes using the laws of physics, which could help with robot arm grasping and placement planning.

lines.say: Let's start with NTT, which has unveiled an AI that predicts when a stack of boxes will collapse before the robot even moves.
lines.show: Let's start with NTT, which has unveiled an AI that predicts stack collapses before a robot moves.

lines.say: By working with physical quantities, it raised the success rate of shelf stacking by a big margin.
lines.show: By working with physical quantities, it raised the shelf stacking success rate by a big margin.

news.label: hdUE is now available
points: Use UE as a Hydra renderer
details: Unreal Engine can be used as an OpenUSD Hydra renderer, and it's released under the MIT license.
From Houdini Solaris or usdview, you can render U S D scenes with Unreal Engine's Lumen or its path tracer.
It's currently a proof of concept for Windows x sixty-four, and the project was released on October twenty-seventh.

news.label: A robot arm that feels weightless
details: The work is split into three parts: reading joint states, calculating gravity torque with Pinocchio, and sending commands to the motors.
It explains concrete details like control cycle jitter and safe stop mechanisms, making it a valuable implementation reference.
The behavior has been verified on devices such as the Jetson Orin Nano.

lines.show: Up next, NVIDIA shows how to build a robot arm that feels weightless and can be moved by hand.

news.label: Gemini on Pixel operates apps
points: Coming to Pixel 10 and 11 in Japan
details: It will roll out gradually to supported models over the next few weeks.
It helps with things like shopping, ride hailing, takeout orders, and restaurant reservations.
Users can check progress and stop the task partway through.

lines.say: And now to Google Pixel. A feature where Gemini operates apps for you has now started in Japan too.

news.label: In-car AI Alpamayo 2 Edge
details: It's a vision language action model that combines a reasoning model with a motion generation model.
During normal driving, it skips unneeded reasoning to cut down on computation.
Optimized for DRIVE AGX Thor, the latency is the time from camera video to generating a driving trajectory.

lines.say: Last up is NVIDIA's in-car AI, Alpamayo two Edge.
lines.show: Last up is NVIDIA's in-car AI, Alpamayo 2 Edge.

lines.say: The technology for running a two billion parameter model inside a car has been released. I love the idea of thinking deeply only when it's needed.
